title: Speak with Us, Lord; Thyself Reveal
description: Speak with Us, Lord; Thyself Reveal in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 522, “For the Divine Presence”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Speak with us, Lord; Thy-self re-veal, While here on earth we rove; Speak to our hearts, and let us feel The kin-dlings of Thy love.

lines: Speak with us, Lord; Thyself reveal,
While here on earth we rove;
Speak to our hearts, and let us feel
All toil and time and care;
Labor is rest, and pain is sweet,
Here then, our God, be pleased to stay,
Our bounding hearts shall own Thy sway,
Thou callest us to seek Thy face;
Thy face, O God, we seek,
Attend the whispers of Thy grace,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
